# Predicting laughter without leaking the future

## TL;DR
A laughter predictor can appear accurate if it sees the response itself. In a synthetic test of 4,096 examples, a leaky model scored .040259 Brier, then .714503 when the post-response marker was flipped. A time-gated model stayed at .175848.

## Problem and reproduction
For behavioral AI engineers: generate three artificial features representing text, prosody and gesture, plus a forbidden post-response marker matching the outcome 96% of the time. Train 4 input arms × 2 seeds × 160 updates on Apple MPS with 8,192 examples. Evaluate a separate 4,096. Reload eight weights and independently audit 72 metrics on CPU. Audio missing means zeroing an artificial feature, not processing actual audio.

![Measured leakage diagnostic and time gate](/assets/research/manager-humor-multimodal-leakage-2026-11-26.svg)

Figure: Brier and prediction-time gate, 2026-11-26, seed42, n=4,096.

| Condition | Brier |
|---|---:|
| Text | 0.235087 |
| Text + audio | 0.193393 |
| All pre-event | 0.175848 |
| Leaky clean | 0.040259 |
| Leaky marker flipped | 0.714503 |
| Pre-event audio missing | 0.221749 |

## Actual public dataset generation
From Humor Transfer Bench (CC BY4.0, 400 prompts, pinned revision 1c2af899), sample one prompt in each of eight domains with seed42. Run local Qwen2.5 0.5B and 1.5B: 16 generations, all nonempty, zero length caps. No humor judgment.

## Trade-offs and unverified work
The synthetic test is cheap and reproducible but cannot establish human validity. Native HumorGen 7B inference remains unrun (BF16 base exceeds local storage); UR-FUNNY data rights are unresolved. No human judgment, intervention effect or model promotion.
